Rashi on Shabbat 82b:1:1.hebrew: היה שלו ושל ע"ז - שהיה חצי מקום הכותל של ע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 82b:1:1.english: [If the wall] belonged to him and to idolatry - That half of the site of the wall belonged to idolatry.

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:1:2.hebrew: נדון מחצה על מחצה - המחצה שלו נחשבת בארבע אמות של כניסה, לפי שחייבוהו חכמים להרחיקו משלו ארבע אמות, וליכנס כולו בתוך שלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 82b:1:2.english: [It] is judged half and half - His half is counted toward the four cubits of withdrawal, because the Sages obligated him to distance it [by taking] four cubits from his own [property], and to enter entirely within his own [property].

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:1:3.hebrew: שקץ תשקצנו - לשון שקץ, כשרץ, שאינו מטמא במשא:
Rashi on Shabbat 82b:1:3.english: You shall utterly detest it - The term *sheketz* [indicates that it is] like a creeping animal, which does not transmit impurity through carrying.

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:1:4.hebrew: נדה מטמאה במשא - אדם הנושאה, דאיתקש לזב: "והדוה בנדתה והזב את זובו וגו'" (ויקרא ט״ו:י׳). וזב מטמא במשא, דכתיב (שם): "וכל הנוגע בכל אשר יהיה תחתיו יטמא עד הערב והנושא אותם וגו'" — אף הזב במשמע אותם:
Rashi on Shabbat 82b:1:4.english: A menstruating woman transmits impurity by carrying - [To] a person who carries her, for she is equated to a zav: "And she that is sick in her impurity, and he that has an issue..." (Leviticus 15:33). And a zav transmits impurity by carrying, as it is written: "And whoever touches anything that was under him shall be impure until the evening, and he that carries them [shall wash his clothes...]" (ibid. 15:10) — the zav is also included in the meaning of "them."

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:2:1.hebrew: באבן מסמא - אבן ששמוה על גבי יתידות וכלים תחתיה — כדכתיב (דניאל ו׳:י״ח): "והיתית אבן חדא ושמת על פום גובא" — ונדה או זב יושבין עליה. אע"פ שלא הכבידו על הכלים, טמאים הכלים, דכתיב: "כל אשר יהיה תחתיו":
Rashi on Shabbat 82b:2:1.english: Regarding an even mesama - A stone that they placed on top of pegs, and vessels are underneath it — as it is written (Daniel 6:18): “And a stone was brought and placed upon the mouth of the pit” — and a menstruating woman [niddah] or a zav sits upon it. Even though they did not press their weight upon the vessels, the vessels are ritually impure, as it is written: “anything that was under him” [Leviticus 15:10].

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:1.english: To [its] accessories - That the vessels used in service [of idolatry] do not transmit impurity, neither through carrying nor through an overlying stone.

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:2.hebrew: למשא - אבל לא לאבן מסמא, דלהכי אהני היקשא דשרץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:2.english: To carrying - But not to an overlying stone [even massema], for to this [end] the juxtaposition to a creeping animal was effective.

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:3.hebrew: ולוקשה לנבלה - דאית בה משא, ולית בה אבן מסמא. והכי עדיף, דתו לא צריך לאקושה לשרץ למעוטי מאבן מסמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:3.english: And let [the Torah] juxtapose it to a carcass - For it transmits [impurity through] carrying, and does not transmit [impurity through] an overriding stone [even masma]. And this would be preferable, since then there would no longer be a need to juxtapose it to a creeping animal to exclude [impurity through] an overriding stone.

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:4.hebrew: אינה לאברים - אם נחתך אבר ממנה, מטמא במשא ובאהל משום תורת אבר מן החי, אבל לא משום תורת אבר מן הנדה. ונפקא מינה — דלא מטמא באבן מסמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:4.english: Does not [transmit impurity] through limbs - If a limb was severed from her, it transmits impurity through carrying and in a tent under the law of a limb from a living [person], but not under the law of a limb of a menstruating woman; and the practical difference is that it does not transmit impurity through an overriding stone.

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:5.hebrew: אף ע"ז אינה לאברים - כגון ע"ז של חוליות, אבר אבר ממנה אינו מטמא כלל משום ע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:5.english: So too, idolatry does not [transmit impurity] through limbs - Such as an idol [made] of joints — each individual limb of it does not transmit impurity at all on account of idolatry.

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:6.english: That which Rav Ḥama asked - Below (Shabbat 83b).

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:7.hebrew: אליבא דרבי עקיבא בעי לה - דאקשה לנדה (למשא): מי אמרינן: להא נמי איתקש? או דילמא: לחומרא מקשינן, לקולא לא מקשינן:
Rashi on Shabbat 82b:3:7.english: He raised the dilemma in accordance with Rabbi Akiva - For [Rabbi Akiva] juxtaposed it to a menstruating woman (for carrying): Do we say that it was juxtaposed for this as well, or perhaps we juxtapose [it] for stringency, [but] we do not juxtapose [it] for leniency?

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:4:1.hebrew: דלא מטמאה - דהא איתקש לשרץ, ובשרץ כתיב מגע ולא כתיב משא:
Rashi on Shabbat 82b:4:1.english: That it does not transmit impurity - For it was juxtaposed to a creeping animal, and regarding a creeping animal, contact is written, but carrying is not written.

Rashi on Shabbat 82b:4:2.english: For wiping with it - It is an answer:

Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:1:1.hebrew: אבניו ועציו ועפריו מטמאים כשרץ - ואפי' למ"ד בפ"ג דמסכת ע"ז (דף מא:): "ע"ז שנשתברה מאליה מותרת" — הא מוקי לה בירושלמי: כגון שהשתחוה לכל אבן ואבן, ולכל עץ ועץ, ולכל עפר ועפר, דהוי ע"ז שלימה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:1:1.english: “Its stones and its wood and its dust transmit impurity like a creeping animal” - And even according to the one who holds in the third chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (41b) that an idol that broke on its own is permitted, behold, the Yerushalmi establishes this [as a case] where one bowed down to each and every stone, and to each and every piece of wood, and to each and every [particle of] dust, such that it is a complete idol.

Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:2:1.hebrew: אמר רבה במשא כ"ע לא פליגי דמטמאה דהא איתקש לנדה - קשה לר"ת: מ"ט דרבנן? אי אית להו הא דאמר בסוף שמעתין (ף כג:): טומאה דע"ז דרבנן היא ולקולא מקשינן — א"כ אמאי מטמאה במשא? נימא: דהיקישא דנדה — דאינה לאיברים, והיקישא דשרץ — דלא מטמאה במשא! ואי סברי רבנן דלחומרא מקשינן — אימא: אהני היקשא דנדה לטמויי באבן מסמא, ודשרץ — לטמויי בכעדשה! ולר' עקיבא נמי, אי לחומרא מקיש — אמאי איצטריך למימר דהיקישא דשרץ למשמשיה? לימא: לטמויי בכעדשה! ואי לקולא מקיש — לא תטמא אפילו במשא, והיקישא דנדה — דאינה לאברים, והיקישא דשרץ — דלא מטמא במשא! וכן לר' אלעזר אליבא דר' עקיבא. ונראה לר"ת, דגרסי' לעיל בספרים: אמר רבה, "תזרם" דאמר קרא — נכרינהו מינך כזר, "צא" תאמר לו — הכנס אל תאמר לו. פירוש: כיון דכתיב כבר ברישא: "וטמאתם את צפוי פסילי כספך" וגו', ל"ל תו למימר "תזרם כמו דוה"? אלא לומר שמאד יש להרחיק. ואתא למימר: אע"ג דשאר קראי נדרשות לקולא, משום דטומאת ע"ז דרבנן — מנדה ילפינן לחומרא. מש"ה קאמר רבה: לכ"ע מטמא במשא, דאית להו דרשא דתזרם. ולרבנן נמי, הוית מטמא באבן מסמא כנדה, אי לאו דממעטין מדאיתקש לשרץ:
Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:2:1.english: Rabba said: With regard to carrying, everyone agrees that it transmits impurity, as it was juxtaposed to a menstruating woman - It is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: What is the reasoning of the Rabbis? If they accept that which [the Gemara] says at the end of our sugya (83b), that the impurity of idolatry is rabbinic and we juxtapose for leniency, if so, why does [idolatry] transmit impurity through carrying? Let us say that the juxtaposition to a menstruating woman [teaches] that it does not [transmit impurity] through limbs, and the juxtaposition to a creeping animal [teaches] that it does not transmit impurity through carrying! And if the Rabbis hold that we juxtapose for stringency, say that the juxtaposition to a menstruating woman is effective to make it transmit impurity via an even masama [an overriding stone], and [the juxtaposition] to a creeping animal to make it transmit impurity with [a piece the size of] a lentil! And according to Rabbi Akiva as well: If he juxtaposes for stringency, why was it necessary to say that the juxtaposition to a creeping animal is for its accessories? Let it say [that it is] to make it transmit impurity with [a piece the size of] a lentil! And if he juxtaposes for leniency, let it not transmit impurity even through carrying, and [explain] the juxtaposition to a menstruating woman [as teaching] that it does not [transmit impurity] through limbs, and the juxtaposition to a creeping animal [as teaching] that it does not transmit impurity through carrying! And so too according to Rabbi Elazar according to Rabbi Akiva. And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that we read in the books earlier: Rabba said: "'You shall scatter them' that the verse states — make them foreign to you like a stranger; 'Go out' you shall say to it — do not say to it 'Enter'." Explanation: Since it is already written in the first part [of the verse], "And you shall defile the overlay of your graven images of silver..." etc., why do I further need [the verse] to say "You shall scatter them like a menstruous woman"? Rather, to say that one must distance [oneself from it] exceedingly. And it comes to say: even though the other verses are expounded for leniency because the impurity of idolatry is rabbinic, from a menstruating woman we derive for stringency. Therefore, Rabba said: according to everyone, it transmits impurity through carrying, as they [all] accept the exposition of "You shall scatter them." And according to the Rabbis as well, it would transmit impurity via an even masama like a menstruating woman, were it not that they exclude [it] from the fact that it was juxtaposed to a creeping animal.

Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:2:2.hebrew: באבן מסמא - פי' בקונטרס: אבן מונחת על גבי יתידות, ונדה יושבת עליה, וכלים תחת האבן, וטמא מ"וכל אשר יהיה תחתיו". וקשה, דבת"כ מפיק אבן מסמא מ"וכל המשכב", וקרא ד"כל אשר יהיה תחתיו" מוקמינן בפרק בנות כותים (נדה לב:) לעליונו של זב, ובת"כ מוקי לה במרכב! ועוד, דאי מ"וכל אשר יהיה תחתיו" נפקא — א"כ אפי' כלים שאין ראוי למשכב ומושב, ובת"כ מוכח בהדיא דכלים שאין ראויין למשכב ומושב אין להם אפי' טומאה קלה! ועוד, אמאי נקט אבן? אפי' דף ע"ג יתידות נמי! ומפרש ר"ת, דאבן מסמא היינו אבן גדולה שהיא כבידה, ואין הכלים מרגישים כובד הזב והנדה מחמת כובד האבן. ומסמא היינו משא גדולה שצריכה שימה, כדכתיב: "והיתית אבן חדא ושמת על פום גובא". אך קשה, דבת"כ מרבה אבן מסמא מ"וכל המשכב", משמע דמרבה מטעם משכב ומושב; ובכל הש"ס משמע דהוי מטעם משא, דבמתני' קרי ליה משא, ובפ' בתרא דנדה (דף כט:) תנן: "הזב והזבה מטמאין במשא", ומפרש בגמרא: מאי משא? אבן מסמא; ובריש דם הנדה [נדה נה.] ממעט מדוה מאבן מסמא מ"והנושא אותם"; ובתוספתא דכלים תניא: "אין טומאה לכלי חרס אלא מאוירו ובהיסט הזב ע"ג אבן מסמא". והיסט [היינו] משא, כדאמר בהעור והרוטב (חולין דף קכד:): "אטו נושא לאו היסט הוא?". משמע: ע"ג אבן מסמא — שהכלים ע"ג האבן, דלא שייך כלל למשכב ומושב; ועוד, דמדרס כלי חרס טהור! וי"ל, דהא דמרבה בת"כ אבן מסמא מטעם משכב ומושב — היינו כשהזב ע"ג האבן והכלים תחתיה; אבל כשיד הטהור או רגלו תחת האבן — הוי מטעם משא, שהטהור נושא את הטמא; או כשאצבעו של זב תחת האבן והכלים עליה — טמא מטעם היסט, דהיינו משא הזב, והיינו היסיט הזב ע"ג אבן מסמא דתוספתא. וא"ת: בריש דם הנדה (נדה דף נד:) דממעט דם הנדה ממשכב ומושב מ"היא יושבת", מאי פריך תו: "אי מה היא מטמאה באבן מסמא אף מדוה נמי מטמאה באבן מסמא"? כיון דכבר מיעט מ"אשר היא יושבת" מדוה ממשכב ומושב, היכי סלקא דעתך תו למימר דמטמא באבן מסמא? ואור"י, דאבן מסמא נפקא לה משום דרשה דלא מטמא אלא אוכלין ומשקין, להכי איצטריך התם למעוטי מדוה אף מאבן מסמא שהיא טומאה קלה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:2:2.english: Via a very heavy stone [even mesama] - Rashi explains in the Kuntres: A stone placed on top of pegs, and a menstruating woman sits upon it, and vessels are beneath the stone, and [the vessel] becomes impure from [the verse], "And whatever is under him [shall be unclean]" (Leviticus 15:10). And this is difficult, for in Torat Kohanim (Sifra), [the law of] an even mesama is derived from "and every bed" (Leviticus 15:5); and the verse of "And whatever is under him" we establish in the chapter [entitled] Benot Kutim (Niddah 32b) as referring to that which is above a zav (elyono shel zav); and in Torat Kohanim it is established as referring to a saddle (merkav)! And furthermore, if it is derived from "And whatever is under him," if so, even vessels that are not fit for lying or sitting [should become impure]; yet in Torat Kohanim it is explicitly proven that vessels that are not fit for lying or sitting do not contract even a light impurity! And furthermore, why did [the Baraita] specify a stone? Even a plank on top of pegs [should] also [transmit impurity in this manner]! And Rabbeinu Tam explains that an even mesama is a large stone that is heavy, such that the vessels do not feel the weight of the zav or the menstruating woman due to the heaviness of the stone. And mesama means a large burden that requires placement (sima), as it is written: "And a stone was brought, and placed [vesumat] upon the mouth of the den" (Daniel 6:18). However, this is difficult: For in Torat Kohanim, an even mesama is included from "and every bed," which implies that it is included by virtue of [the law of] lying and sitting (mishkav umoshav); whereas throughout the Talmud it implies that it is by virtue of [the law of] carrying (massa)! For in the Mishnah it calls it massa; and in the last chapter of Niddah (29b) we learned: "The zav and the zavah transmit impurity through massa," and the Gemara explains: What is massa? An even mesama; and at the beginning of [the chapter] Dam HaNiddah [Niddah 55a], it excludes a dava [a menstruant] from [transmitting impurity via] an even mesama from [the verse], "And whoever carries them" (Leviticus 15:10); and in the Tosefta of Keilim it is taught: "There is no impurity for an earthenware vessel except from its airspace and through the shifting [heyset] of a zav on top of an even mesama." And shifting [is] carrying, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] Ha'Or VehaRotev (Chullin 124b): "Is one who carries not shifting?" "On top of an even mesama" implies that the vessels are on top of the stone, where [the law of] lying and sitting (mishkav umoshav) does not apply at all; and furthermore, earthenware vessels are not subject to midras impurity! And it can be answered that that which Torat Kohanim includes an even mesama by virtue of [the law of] lying and sitting is when the zav is on top of the stone and the vessels are beneath it. But when the hand or foot of the ritually pure person is beneath the stone, it is by virtue of carrying (massa), for the pure person is carrying the impure person; or when the finger of the zav is beneath the stone and the vessels are on top of it, [the vessel] becomes impure by virtue of shifting (heyset), which is carrying (massa) by the zav; and this is "the shifting of the zav on top of an even mesama" of the Tosefta. And if you will say: At the beginning of [the chapter] Dam HaNiddah (Niddah 54b), where it excludes the blood of a menstruating woman from [the law of] lying and sitting (mishkav umoshav) from [the verse], "[any article that] she sits [upon]" (Leviticus 15:20), why does it ask further: "If just as she transmits impurity via an even mesama, so too should a dava [her blood] transmit impurity via an even mesama?" Since it already excluded a dava [her blood] from lying and sitting from "that she sits upon," how could it enter your mind to say further that it transmits impurity via an even mesama? And the Ri explains that an even mesama is derived based on an exposition that it transmits impurity only to food and drink; therefore it was necessary there to exclude a dava even from an even mesama, which is a light impurity.

Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:2:3.hebrew: ורבנן סברי כשרץ כו' - וא"ת: אמאי איצטריך שרץ למעוטי אבן מסמא? תיפוק ליה מדאיתקש למת (לקמן שבת דף פג:)! וי"ל: דכיון דגלי לן קרא דנכרינהו מינך כזר, דאית לן לאקשויי לנדה לחומרא — לא הוה ממעטי ממת אבן מסמא בע"ז, כיון דאיצטריך היקישא דמת לשיעור כזית; א"נ, לכדאמר בפרק נגמר הדין (סנהדרין דף מז:): "מה ע"ז במחובר לא מיתסרא, אף קבר במחובר לא מיתסר":
Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:2:3.english: "And the Rabbis hold [it is] like a creeping animal," etc. - And if you say: Why was [a comparison to] a creeping animal needed to exclude a heavy stone [even mesama]? Let him derive it from [the fact] that it is juxtaposed to a corpse (below, Shabbat 83b)! And it can be said: Since the verse revealed to us to "make them foreign to you like a stranger," [indicating] that we are to juxtapose it to a menstruating woman for stringency, we would not have excluded a heavy stone [even mesama] in [the case of] idolatry from [the juxtaposition to] a corpse, since the juxtaposition to a corpse was needed for the measure of an olive-bulk; or alternatively, for that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Nigmar HaDin (Sanhedrin 47b): "Just as idolatry [that is] attached [to the ground] is not forbidden, so too a grave [that is] attached [to the ground] is not forbidden."

Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:3:1.hebrew: ולרבי עקיבא למאי הלכתא איתקש לשרץ כו' - תימה לר"י: מאי קמיבעיא ליה? הא איצטריך לאפוקי שלא יטמא באהל המת — דמנדה דילמא לא ילפינן שום קולא, דהא בעי רב חמא בר גוריא בסמוך: אי ישנה לאברים, אע"ג דנדה אינה לאברים! ויש לומר, דלענין דליכא בע"ז חומרא דמת, שפיר ילפינן מנדה; ואע"ג דהיקישא דנדה לחומרא, קולא נמי אית לן למילף. והא דמספקא ליה לענין אברים — משום דלא דמי: דאברי נדה אין אדם יכול להחזירם, ואברי ע"ז מיהא אומן יכול להחזירם. א"נ, הא דקאמר "למאי הלכתא", וכן הא דקא משני "למשמשין", היינו: את"ל דילפינן קולא מנדה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:3:1.english: "And according to Rabbi Akiva, for what halakha was it juxtaposed to a creeping animal, etc." - The Ri is puzzled: What is [the Gemara's] question? Surely [the juxtaposition to a creeping animal] was needed to exclude [idolatry], so that it does not transmit impurity in a tent [like] a corpse — for from a menstruating woman, perhaps we do not derive any leniency, as Rav Ḥama bar Guria asks nearby: Is it subject to [impurity through severed] limbs, even though a menstruating woman is not subject to [impurity through severed] limbs! And one can say that with regard to [the fact] that idolatry does not have the stringency of a corpse, we properly derive [that] from a menstruating woman; and even though the juxtaposition to a menstruating woman is for stringency, we also derive a leniency. And that which was a dilemma to him regarding [severed] limbs is because they are not comparable: for the limbs of a menstruating woman, a person cannot reattach them, whereas the limbs of an idol, at any rate, a craftsman can reattach them. Alternatively, that which [the Gemara] asks, "For what halakha [was it juxtaposed to a creeping animal]?", and similarly that which it answers, "[To teach regarding] its accessories," is [only] if you say that we derive a leniency from a menstruating woman.

Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:3:2.hebrew: למשמשיה - פירש בקונטרס: שאין כלים המשמשין לע"ז מטמאין, לא במשא ולא באבן מסמא. משמע, דאי לאו דאיתקש לשרץ, הוו מטמי כע"ז באבן מסמא. ותימה: דלרבנן, דהיקישא דשרץ לא אתא למשמשיה, מנלן דמשמשין לא מטמו במשא כמו ע"ז עצמה? דלקמן קאמר רב אשי אליבא דרבה: "משמשין, בין הן שהסיטו אחרים בין אחרים שהסיטו אותן — טהורין"! ונראה לר"י, דאי לאו דאיתקש משמשין לשרץ, לא הוה מטמינן להו כלל. ורבנן דמטמו למשמשיה — מדכתיב: "שקץ תשקצנו כי חרם הוא", משמע: כל דבר שהוא חרם, פירש שאסור בהנאה, הוי כשרץ; ומשמשין אסור בהנאה. ובזה לא יתיישב פי' הקונטרס, דמכי חרם הוא לא משמע למעוטי משמשין דלא מטמו במשא, דאין שום יתור לכך; אבל הא דמשמשיה טמא — משתמע שפיר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:3:2.english: To its accessories - Rashi explained that the vessels that serve idolatry do not transmit impurity either through carrying or through an overlying stone. This implies that had it not been juxtaposed to a creeping animal, they would transmit impurity like idolatry [itself], through an overlying stone. And this is astonishing: for according to the Rabbis, for whom the juxtaposition to a creeping animal did not come [to apply] to its accessories, from where do we know that accessories do not transmit impurity through carrying like idolatry itself? For later (83b), Rav Ashi says in accordance with Rabbah: "Accessories, whether they moved others or others moved them, are pure!" And it appears to the Ri that had accessories not been juxtaposed to a creeping animal, we would not have rendered them impure at all. And the Rabbis, who consider its accessories impure — [derive this] from that which is written: "You shall utterly detest it, for it is a banned thing" (Deuteronomy 7:26). This implies: anything that is a banned thing — meaning, that is forbidden from benefit — is like a creeping animal; and accessories [of idolatry] are forbidden from benefit. And with this, Rashi's explanation is not resolved, because from "for it is a banned thing" it is not implied to exclude accessories [such] that they would not transmit impurity through carrying, as there is no superfluity for that; however, that its accessories are impure is well implied.

Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:3:3.hebrew: ולוקשה רחמנא לנבלה - אמאי דהוקשה למת ליכא למיפרך דלוקש לנבלה, דהא איצטריך למת לכדדרשינן בנגמר הדין. ובקונט' פי' דהכי פריך: "ולוקשה לנבלה" — משום דאז לא הוה צריך לאקושה לשרץ:
Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:3:3.english: "And let the Merciful One juxtapose it to a carcass" - Regarding that which [idolatry] was juxtaposed to a corpse, one cannot object that it should be juxtaposed to a carcass, for [the juxtaposition to] a corpse was necessary for that which we expound in [the chapter entitled] Negmar HaDin. And in the Kunteres [Rashi] explained that this is what [the Gemara] is asking: "And let [the Torah] juxtapose it to a carcass" — because then it would not have needed to juxtapose it to a creeping animal.

Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:4:1.hebrew: ורבי אלעזר אמר כו' - פי' רבינו שמואל, דבמילתיה דר' אלעזר ל"ג: "ור"ע למאי הלכתא איתקש לשרץ? למשמשיה", דהא איצטריך למעוטה מאבן מסמא, כדאמר: "דכ"ע לא פליגי דלא מטמא באבן מסמא, דהא איתקש לשרץ". ויש ספרים דל"ג "דהא איתקש לשרץ", ולפי זה מצינן למימר דטעמא דר' אלעזר דכ"ע לא פליגי דלא מטמא באבן מסמא לאו משום דאיתקש לשרץ, אלא בלא שום יתור לא מחמרינן כולי האי לטמאות באבן מסמא; ולפי זה גרסי' שפיר: "ור"ע למאי הלכתא כו'". והא דפריך בתר הכי: "ולוקשה רחמנא לנבלה" — לא פריך "לוקשה לנבלה, ותו לא צריך לאקושה לשרץ", דהשתא נמי לא צריך לאקושי משום הכי לשרץ; אלא הכי פריך: דהוה ליה טפי לאקושה לנבלה, דדמיא ממש לנבלה, אבל לנדה לא דמיא, דנדה מטמאה באבן מסמא, משא"כ בע"ז:
Tosafot on Shabbat 82b:4:1.english: "And Rabbi Elazar said, etc." - Rabbeinu Shmuel explained that in the statement of Rabbi Elazar we do not read: "And according to Rabbi Akiva, for what halakha was it juxtaposed to a creeping animal? For its accessories," because [that juxtaposition] was needed to exclude it from [transmitting impurity through] an overlying stone, as [the Gemara] says: "for everyone agrees that it does not transmit impurity through an overlying stone, as it was juxtaposed to a creeping animal." And there are texts that do not read "as it was juxtaposed to a creeping animal"; and according to this, we can say that Rabbi Elazar's reasoning that everyone agrees that it does not transmit impurity through an overlying stone is not because it was juxtaposed to a creeping animal, but rather, without any superfluous [derivation], we do not impose such a stringency as to transmit impurity through an overlying stone; and according to this, we properly read: "And according to Rabbi Akiva, for what halakha, etc." And that which [the Gemara] asks after this: "And let the Merciful One juxtapose it to a carcass!" — it is not asking: "Let [the Torah] juxtapose it to a carcass, and furthermore it would no longer be necessary to juxtapose it to a creeping animal," since even now it does not need to be juxtaposed to a creeping animal for that reason; rather, this is what it asks: it should rather have juxtaposed it to a carcass, because it truly resembles a carcass, whereas it does not resemble a menstruating woman, for a menstruating woman transmits impurity through an overlying stone, which is not the case with idolatry.
